dramatic_truth: Stranded in Merecross, Greg enters a civic access meeting as an outside user perspective and discovers the useful intervention is often routing existing complaints to the people who can act on them.
performance: He repeatedly bounds his authority, reports only his own crutch experience and Carrow procedures, and refuses to become carpenter or access specialist.
screenplay: North Civic Hall meeting; ornamental rail grip reproduces a patron complaint; complaints ledger reveals repeated access reports never routed to maintenance; carpenter and records staff finally meet around actual evidence; Civic offers paid site walkthroughs.
prose_comparison: Institutional dialogue and procedural detail are the scene: Greg adds outside perspective but the system changes because local records meet local authority.

dramatic_truth: Greg works a Merecross public-site walkthrough with local cane user Dema Orr, making outside perspective useful only when paired with local operational knowledge rather than substituted for it.
performance: Dema and Greg catch different barriers, route lighting and surface questions to proper crews, and jointly refuse to treat early Glasswake behavior as explanation-ready.
screenplay: Market terrace walkthrough; local user and visiting crutch user compare route friction; lantern frames rotate unexpectedly under early Glass pull; Maro isolates an old mirror flake without claiming cause; field-crew opportunity enters Greg's horizon.
prose_comparison: The chapter establishes local/visitor complementarity and lets Merecross become socially specific rather than generic travel backdrop.

dramatic_truth: Greg applies for Vessa Harn's River Survey record-hand slot because he wants the farther work, while fully exposing his physical constraints and refusing to convert old S-class experience into automatic qualification.
performance: He asks terrain, skiff, load, pay, field-system, and personal-artifact questions before applying; Merecross pre-wake market temptation remains separate from job choice.
screenplay: Field notice investigated; Vessa gives exact requirements; Greg files application; Night Rest remains unaffordable and visibly wake-sensitive; letter home makes the choice emotionally real.
prose_comparison: The long pre-application inquiry is the mature opposite of impulsive adventure acceptance and materially changes Greg's geographic ambition.

dramatic_truth: On his deliberate rest day before the field trial, Greg learns that not monetizing every hour can coexist with useful civic action when Glasswake and a cart accident intrude.
performance: He plays with children, stays behind public procedure during a strange drain-light run, then braces a failing cargo load only within a role his body and available rated bollard can safely support.
screenplay: Bad packing rehearsal; city wandering; children's ring game; first drain-light run; municipal workers document; festival cart loses wheel; Greg braces rope through known tie post, resets when crutch slips, and stops once porter is freed.
prose_comparison: The apparent wandering is deliberate decompression and then a test of whether Greg can help without turning every anomaly into his investigation.

dramatic_truth: Vessa's trial tests whether Greg's current body and current habits fit River Survey work, including the crucial ability to declare limits before they become crew problems.
performance: Greg copies uncertainty rather than cleaning it, requests an approved carry solution rather than one-crutching gravel, asks for assistance on skiff transfer, and accepts leaving the uncertain oval in a lockbox.
screenplay: Writing/read-back test; eight-pound case carry with harness; route and cart transfer; skiff transfer; second candidate Orin arrives late; Greg produces an unplanned clean external effect on a rolling gauge marker and deliberately refuses immediate repetition.
prose_comparison: Trial repetition differentiates skill dimensions and makes the spontaneous magic result meaningful precisely because Greg does not chase it.

dramatic_truth: Greg begins local paid prep work with Dask and learns Merecross gauge systems by recording what each housing actually says rather than trying to own the broader Glasswake model.
performance: He copies dictated readings, preserves uncertainty, routes permit obstruction correctly, reports crutch-tip vibration as a separate tactile observation, and begins fitting into crew banter without losing scope.
screenplay: Gauge stations one through twelve; secondary returns appear; freight cart blocks one housing; permit retrieved; tactile three-two pulse noted but not investigated; floodgate produces stronger multi-return response and crew converges.
prose_comparison: Station repetition builds system literacy, crew relationships, and uncertainty discipline; every station changes the evidence state.

dramatic_truth: Greg and Orin become genuine competing candidates while also functioning as crewmates, each covering different strengths without hiding the other's competence.
performance: They retrieve reserve equipment together, independently witness a terrace response, handle Glasswake-distorted stairs, report each other's strengths honestly, and refuse to steal credit.
screenplay: Platform setup; custody mismatch stops board install; stamped reserve retrieved; black pocket and sequential rail tones interrupt route; service stairs reveal visual edge distortion; Vessa asks each candidate to assess the other.
prose_comparison: Competition and cooperation coexist in the same operational beats, which is the character result; compressing the work would flatten that tension.

dramatic_truth: Glasswake's first full night stress-tests both candidates under real workload, and Greg wins the field slot because his strongest trait is disciplined uncertainty rather than speed or spectacle.
performance: He takes bodily rest before failure, handles crowd pressure without overclaiming, reports the oval's cold response without using it, and keeps observation separate from interpretation during spectacular river events.
screenplay: First Wake workday; Greg and Orin admit competitive feelings; floodgate strong response; spontaneous station bells and dark threshold-shaped interruption; crowd held; Vessa chooses Greg for record slot and offers Orin real local work.
prose_comparison: The long festival shift is the proof environment for the hiring decision. The decision would feel arbitrary without the accumulated performed behavior.

dramatic_truth: Greg formally joins River Survey and leaves Merecross with a crew, while demonstrating that old S-class method remains available as a selective mode rather than his default way of living.
performance: He uses high-output attention briefly to solve cart manifest geometry, then explicitly declines to live in that mode; he receives six-copper start pay only at crew roll and enters the road as current-body worker.
screenplay: Post-wake repack; Greg locks in on load distribution; Vessa discusses when that mode is useful; crew roll signed; six copper paid; road causeway visual displacement handled by existing road-reader system; crew transfers to skiff.
prose_comparison: The chapter converts abstract old competence into a bounded operational tool and marks the actual transition from applicant to traveling field worker.

dramatic_truth: Greg begins true field travel as a passenger inside a competent ensemble and discovers reserves of skill, money, and future power are valuable partly because he does not have to spend them constantly.
performance: He lets the crew own river roles, watches without converting idle travel into mandatory optimization, and refuses to volunteer into a new Alder Basin industrial spill before route authority is established.
screenplay: Skiff travel toward Alder Basin; post-Glasswake river ecology; Survey House arrival; return-lime spill may implicate retired glass-lock Four-C; route waits for field reader; Greg browses cheap industrial detectors but buys nothing.
prose_comparison: Quiet travel and reserve reflection are thematic payoff to the capital-discipline arc, while the new spill opens field stakes without forcing Greg into ownership.
